exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean vs. planned induction of labor)
outcome: composite of neonatal outcomes (preoperative inhaled nitric oxide use, inotrope use, preoperative mortality, reoperation, readmission, delayed sternal closure, diaphragmatic paralysis, postoperative mortality)
composite neurological morbidity (hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy, seizures, intraventricular hemorrhage, stroke)
cohort: The study included 90 neonates with prenatally diagnosed d-Transposition of the Great Arteries (d-TGA) with an intact ventricular septum (IVS) who received surgical care at a single tertiary care referral center from 2020 to 2023.
finding: Neonates with prenatally diagnosed d-TGA with an IVS had similar surgical outcomes regardless of delivery time at the single tertiary care center.
mod_finding: There was no statistically significant difference in primary neonatal outcomes between cesarean and planned induction of labor, nor between daytime and after-hours deliveries for neonates with d-TGA with an IVS.
